subject.title: fix: beta releases require manual reruns after plugin publication

question: Should default beta publication be allowed to finish as `beta-live` while packaged-upgrade proof and plugin npm/ClawHub convergence continue asynchronously, rather than retaining the existing all-ecosystem blocking completion contract?
rationale: The patch intentionally changes release success semantics and operator recovery expectations; code review can verify mechanics but cannot choose the permanent beta release policy.

options.title: Approve asynchronous beta convergence
options.body: Allow beta core publication after core proof, with a clearly documented beta-live state and an owned continuation that completes or reports ecosystem convergence.

options.title: Keep ecosystem convergence blocking
options.body: Require plugin npm, ClawHub, and packaged-upgrade completion before beta release success, while retaining only safe retry and evidence-reuse improvements.

options.title: Make the policy opt-in
options.body: Keep the current blocking default and expose asynchronous convergence only through an explicit release-controller option until operational experience validates it.

recommendation.title: Approve asynchronous beta convergence
recommendation.body: Allow beta core publication after core proof, with a clearly documented beta-live state and an owned continuation that completes or reports ecosystem convergence.

likelyOwner.reason: The available history identifies this contributor as the active author of the affected release orchestration; final policy approval still needs the release-owner group represented by the protected label.
